The platform readiness gates constitute a Boolean lattice defining system capabilities. Each gate acts as a binary switch that either enables or disables core functionalities such as scoring, pick persistence, and derived history access. These gates are implemented as immutable configuration flags within the PlatformConfig object, ensuring consistency across workers, API routes, and content generation modules. The logical structure supports a dual-state system: either a functionality is fully available or it is entirely disabled, preventing partial or inconsistent behavior. In GSI, these gates constrain inference by filtering out bootstrap-era data and enforcing outcome-validation before learning. In GSE, they govern state transitions and resource allocation during runtime. Failure modes occur when gates are misconfigured or when dependencies between gates are violated, leading to cascading errors in downstream systems.
